walkthrough:
Set $y = \frac{2x}{3x - 1}$ and cross-multiply to isolate $x$:
$$y(3x - 1) = 2x \implies 3xy - y = 2x$$
$$3xy - 2x = y \implies x(3y - 2) = y$$
$$x = \frac{y}{3y - 2}$$

Write down the inverse function in terms of $x$:
$$f^{-1}(x) = \frac{x}{3x - 2}$$

hints: Combine fractions on the LHS over $3(3x - 1)$ to show $\frac{6x}{3(3x - 1)} = \frac{2x}{3x - 1}$.
walkthrough:
Combine the two terms over the common denominator $3(3x - 1)$:
$$\frac{2}{3} + \frac{2}{3(3x - 1)} = \frac{2(3x - 1) + 2}{3(3x - 1)} = \frac{6x - 2 + 2}{3(3x - 1)}$$

Simplify the numerator and cancel the common factor of $3$:
$$\frac{6x}{3(3x - 1)} = \frac{2x}{3x - 1}$$

Using the alternative form $f(x) = \frac{2}{3} + \frac{2}{3(3x - 1)}$ on the domain $x > \frac{1}{3}$:
Since $x > \frac{1}{3} \implies 3x - 1 > 0$, the second term $\frac{2}{3(3x - 1)}$ is strictly positive and can take any value in $(0, \infty)$.
$$\text{Range of } f: \quad f(x) > \frac{2}{3} \quad \left(\text{or } \left(\frac{2}{3}, \infty\right)\right)$$
